placements.why: Both segments concern instrument calibration — the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibrated at 88.4 MHz and verified against June reference plates. No existing strata category covers this organizational domain; Calibration is the natural container for calibration-related content that future envelopes may feed.
placements.title: Calibration established by reference verification, not bare assertion
placements.frame: What reference standards and verification procedures ratify an instrument's calibration, and what authority does that ratification carry for downstream observations?

placements.title: Calibration authority performed through reference-plate verification
placements.frame: How does citing verification against an established reference standard perform calibration authority rather than merely asserting it?
placements.why: Both expressions carry the same thematic content: calibration authority is established by verification against June reference plates, not by bare assertion. src-1 carries this as Quill's expert claim ('verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it holds across the full observing band'), while src-2 re-encodes it as a settled decision record. The theme — that calibration authority is performed through reference verification — is a subject future envelopes could feed, not a one-time fact.
